function RunInspector(props: {
  project: WorkshopProject;
  run: MakerRun;
  busy: boolean;
  streamError: string | null;
  cancel: () => void;
  reconcile: () => void;
  retry: () => void;
}) {
  const [now, setNow] = useState(Date.now());
  useEffect(() => {
    if (["SUCCEEDED", "FAILED", "CANCELLED"].includes(props.run.status)) return;
    const timer = window.setInterval(() => setNow(Date.now()), 1_000);
    return () => window.clearInterval(timer);
  }, [props.run.status]);
  const terminal = ["SUCCEEDED", "FAILED", "CANCELLED"].includes(props.run.status);
  const elapsed = Math.max(0, (props.run.finishedAt ? Date.parse(props.run.finishedAt) : now) - Date.parse(props.run.startedAt ?? props.run.createdAt));
  const last = props.run.events.at(-1);
  return (
    <section className="run-inspector" aria-live="polite" aria-label="Run Inspector">
      <div className="run-inspector-heading">
        <div>
          <p className="eyebrow">Run Inspector</p>
          <h2>Maker · {props.run.status.replaceAll("_", " ")}</h2>
        </div>
        <span className="meta">{formatDuration(elapsed)} elapsed</span>
      </div>
      <p>{last?.summary ?? "The saved run has no events yet."}</p>
      {props.streamError ? <p className="banner bad">Live updates disconnected: {props.streamError} Reconnecting from event {props.run.lastEventSequence}.</p> : null}
      {props.run.failureCode === "AUTHENTICATION" ? (
        <p className="banner bad">Repair OpenCode authentication by matching `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` with the server password, then reconcile or start a new run.</p>
      ) : null}
      <ol className="run-events">
        {props.run.events.slice(-50).map((event) => (
          <li key={event.id}>
            <span className="meta">#{event.sequence} · {event.category} · {new Date(event.timestamp).toLocaleTimeString()}</span>
            <div>{event.summary}</div>
          </li>
        ))}
      </ol>
      {props.run.result ? (
        <div className="run-evidence">
          <h3>Final evidence</h3>
          <p>{props.run.result.summary}</p>
          {props.run.result.files.length ? (
            <ul>{props.run.result.files.map((file) => <li key={file.path}>{file.status} {file.path} (+{file.additions}/-{file.deletions})</li>)}</ul>
          ) : <p>No file-change evidence is available.</p>}
          {props.run.result.verification ? (
            <p>Verification: {props.run.result.verification.status} · exit {props.run.result.verification.exitCode ?? "unavailable"}</p>
          ) : <p>Verification evidence is unavailable.</p>}
          {props.run.result.model ? <p>Model: {props.run.result.model.providerID}/{props.run.result.model.id} · cost {props.run.result.cost ?? "unknown"}</p> : null}
          {props.run.result.limitation ? <p className="banner">Limitation: {props.run.result.limitation}</p> : null}
        </div>
      ) : null}
      <div className="actions">
        {!terminal && props.run.status !== "UNKNOWN" ? (
          <button className="action secondary" type="button" disabled={props.busy || Boolean(props.run.cancelRequestedAt)} onClick={props.cancel}>
            {props.run.cancelRequestedAt ? "Cancellation pending" : "Cancel native run"}
          </button>
        ) : null}
        {props.run.status === "UNKNOWN" ? (
          <button className="action" type="button" disabled={props.busy} onClick={props.reconcile}>Reconcile saved session</button>
        ) : null}
        {(props.run.status === "FAILED" || props.run.status === "CANCELLED") && props.project.stage === "MAKER" ? (
          <button className="action" type="button" disabled={props.busy} onClick={props.retry}>Start a new run</button>
        ) : null}
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}

function formatDuration(milliseconds: number): string {
  const seconds = Math.floor(milliseconds / 1_000);
  const minutes = Math.floor(seconds / 60);
  return minutes ? `${minutes}m ${seconds % 60}s` : `${seconds}s`;
}

function Activity({ project }: { project: WorkshopProject }) {
  const latest = [...project.operations].reverse().slice(0, 4);
  return (

# OpenCode integration

Status: canonical implemented integration contract  
Last verified: 31 October 2026 (IST)

This document owns OpenCode-specific facts. It does not authorize provider login, account changes, inference, or credential handling.

## Supported baseline

| Item | Inspected fact | Compatibility statement |
|---|---|---|
| Node | `package.json` requires `>=22.14.0`; Render pins `22.14.0`; Phase 0 ran on `22.14.0` | Node 22.14.0 is the verified baseline. Later Node releases are not proven by Phase 0. |
| OpenCode client | `@opencode/client` is lockfile-pinned to `2.0.32` | 2.0.32 is the supported client baseline. |
| Hosted OpenCode binary | `@opencode/cli-linux-x64-baseline` is lockfile-pinned to `2.0.32` | Render starts this exact Linux x64 baseline package. |
| Local CLI | Safe preflight found `opencode 2.0.32` on PATH | CLI startup and `serve --help` passed; no server/model session was started. |
| Server response | `nativeEngineStatusSchema` accepts a version matching `2.x` | This broad validation is not evidence that every 2.x release is compatible. Re-verify before changing either pin. |
| Model | Hard-coded `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` | Availability, free pricing, and behavior are unstable external facts; Phase 0 did not perform inference. |

The preflight also found an adjacent legacy `@opencode-ai/sdk 1.18.26` and correctly marked it inconclusive. Application code imports only `@opencode/client`; the adjacent package is not the declared application contract.

## Connection and credential ownership

- Local OpenCode is expected at `OPENCODE_BASE_URL`, defaulting to `http://127.0.0.1:4096`.
- When `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` is set, the server sends HTTP Basic Auth using username `opencode`. OpenCode must be started with the matching server password.
- Provider/model credentials and provider login state belong to OpenCode. They are not copied into browser storage or project state.
- The application server reads the OpenCode password from its environment. The browser never receives it.
- Render starts OpenCode as a child process with matching `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` and `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD`, plus persistent XDG data/config directories.

Current operator steps remain in [SENTRY_AND_OPENCODE_SETUP.md](SENTRY_AND_OPENCODE_SETUP.md) until `docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md` is created with a verified onboarding flow.

## API surface used

The application currently uses:

- server information and model catalog for `/api/engine`;
- session create/get, prompt/generate/wait, and message list;
- session diff after Maker work; and
- session get/outcome for reconciliation.

Oracle, Architect, and Witness create read-only sessions in `spirit-workspace`. Maker creates an edit-capable, shell-denied session in `demo-workspace`. A saved session id is reused for Oracle, Architect, and Maker; Witness deliberately starts fresh for evidence review.

## Current operation behavior

- `speak` first calls synchronous generation. If the returned text is shorter than 80 characters, it sends a prompt, waits for idle with a 90-second deadline, and reconstructs assistant text from message history.
- `perform` prompts Maker and waits in the same API request for idle or a 180-second timer. It then checks model/cost and asks OpenCode for the session diff.
- A Maker timeout does not interrupt the native session. If no diff is visible, the operation is stored as failed; network-like failures are stored as `UNKNOWN` but may lack a native session id.
- The current cancel endpoint changes only application state for a stored non-terminal operation. It does not invoke an OpenCode abort/interrupt API.
- Reconciliation calls session get and maps native succeeded/failed/interrupted/running/idle information to the saved application operation. No event subscription is used.

## Authentication and failure states

| Failure | Current signal | Recovery today |
|---|---|---|
| Server stopped/wrong URL | Engine 503 or network-like operation error | Start OpenCode or correct server environment, then make a new request only when no unknown operation needs reconciliation. |
| Missing/wrong password | OpenCode request failure | Match `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` with the OpenCode server password and retry. The UI does not yet identify auth separately. |
| Model absent | `modelAvailable: false` with a fixed-model limitation | Configure OpenCode so the exact model appears. Substitution is rejected. |
| Model/cost changes during a session | Operation throws after session inspection | Inspect OpenCode/provider state; do not claim a free successful run. |
| Timeout/disconnect | Application records `UNKNOWN` when classified as network-like | Reconcile only when a native session id was saved; do not blindly repeat. |
| Malformed model output | Schema error; bounded Architect/Witness prose fallback in some cases | Revise/retry without treating text as approval. |

## Trust and privacy

- OpenCode and its configured model provider receive runtime prompts and the selected workshop context. “Local browser” does not mean inference stays on the device.
- Model output, messages, errors, and diffs are untrusted. Zod schemas and workflow transitions—not model prose—control approval and stage changes.
- Native permissions are defense-in-depth around workspace selection. The checked-in fixture test validates its fixture shape, but Phase 0 did not repeat a live OpenCode edit/denial proof.
- Sentry agent spans record role, conversation/session/message identifiers, model name, cost metadata, and tool names. Instrumentation disables GenAI inputs/outputs and request secrets.

## Re-verification triggers

Re-run official API/version checks and an opt-in live compatibility diagnostic before changing the OpenCode/client version, permission shape, session/event APIs, model/provider policy, authentication method, timeout/retry policy, or hosted process model. Record the result here, the system effect in Architecture, setup impact in Local Setup/Hosted Deployment, recovery impact in Operations, and the release note in Changelog.
# Operations and recovery

Status: canonical state, backup, migration, and recovery policy  
Last verified: 31 October 2026 (IST)

This document owns persisted-state operations. The rules below are binding prerequisites for later schema changes; Phase 0 does not alter user data or implement a migration runner.

## Current persisted state

`UB_DATA_DIR` defaults to `.unfinished-business/`. The application currently manages:

```text
UB_DATA_DIR/
  project.json
  project.json.previous
  demo-workspace/
  spirit-workspace/
```

Render additionally keeps OpenCode XDG data and config under `/var/data`. Secrets remain environment-owned and are not part of a repository backup.

`project.json` uses `schemaVersion: 1` and a monotonically increasing `revision`. Its validated record contains project identity/workspace, workflow stage, sections and approvals, idempotent actions, operations, evidence, next action, product and Maker approvals, capped transcript, capabilities, Witness drafts, and native session references.

Current saves are temporary-file-plus-rename writes with a one-generation `.previous` copy. Current loads fall back to `.previous` when the primary file cannot be parsed or validated. This is crash recovery, not a sufficient backup or migration system.

Phase 0 validated the existing local primary record read-only as schema v1/revision 6 and the previous snapshot as schema v1/revision 5. It did not print user text, migrate, repair, or write either file. This is inspection evidence, not a promise that those revisions remain current after later application use.

## Versioning rules

1. `schemaVersion` is a required positive integer at the root of every durable project record. Version 1 remains the only implemented version in Phase 0.
2. A code change that changes required fields, field meaning, enum meaning, identity, or durable invariants must increment the schema version. Adding a Zod default alone does not waive migration review.
3. Migrations are forward-only, explicit, deterministic functions `N -> N+1`. The application must chain them one version at a time and validate after every step.
4. A migration must preserve ids, approvals, hashes, revisions, evidence provenance, operation/native-session references, and user text unless the corresponding decision entry explicitly documents a loss and recovery path.
5. Unsupported newer versions fail closed with an actionable message. They must never be coerced into an older schema or overwritten.
6. Migration code performs no inference, network requests, provider login, deployment action, or external account mutation.
7. A migration is complete only with fixtures for every supported source version, success tests, interrupted-write recovery, corrupt-input preservation, idempotent restart behavior, and documented rollback limits.

## Backup-before-migration rules

Before the first write by code that can migrate durable state:

1. Stop mutations or acquire an exclusive data-directory lock.
2. Read bytes without modifying the source and validate/detect the source version.
3. Create a uniquely named, timestamped backup outside the replacement path. Include `project.json`, its `.previous` snapshot, and any workspace/native metadata whose identifiers the migrated record references. For a private hosted instance, take a provider disk/snapshot backup when supported as well.
4. Record the source schema, application version/commit, size, and a cryptographic checksum in a backup manifest. Never include environment secrets in that manifest.
5. Verify the backup can be read before migration continues.
6. Write the migrated record to a new temporary file, validate it completely, flush it as supported, and atomically rename it into place. Preserve corrupt or rejected inputs under a quarantine name; never overwrite them with a default project.
7. Keep the migration backup until the new version has passed its documented validation window. Retention and pruning must be explicit and must never delete the last known-good backup.

The existing `project.json.previous` file does not satisfy these rules: it has no unique generation, manifest, checksum, retention guarantee, or workspace/OpenCode coverage.

## Forward migration and rollback

- Startup may automatically migrate only versions explicitly listed as supported by the running build. It must surface that a backup and migration occurred.
- If any step fails, leave the original and backup untouched, quarantine partial output, and refuse mutations. Do not initialize a blank project over recoverable data.
- Rollback means stopping the application and restoring a verified pre-migration backup with the application version that understands it. Never run older code against state already written by newer code.
- A successful migration is not reversed in place. Corrections are a new forward migration.
- OpenCode session ids may outlive application migration but are external references; inability to inspect an old session must become an honest limitation, not deletion of local evidence.

## Current recovery matrix

| Symptom | Safe current action | Do not do |
|---|---|---|
| `project.json` invalid but `.previous` valid | Stop writes, copy both files to an operator backup, inspect the load source, and restore deliberately. | Do not delete the primary or assume fallback is a migration. |
| Both project files invalid | Preserve both and logs, stop the app, and diagnose against schema v1. | Do not let startup replace them with a new project. |
| Revision conflict | Reload project state and reapply the user's intended change to the new revision. | Do not bypass the expected revision. |
| Duplicate action id/same payload | Treat the returned state as the idempotent result. | Do not invoke OpenCode again. |
| Duplicate action id/different payload | Generate a new action id after reviewing intent. | Do not reuse the id or overwrite its ledger entry. |
| Native operation unknown | Reconcile the saved native session before retrying. | Do not start a duplicate run merely because the browser disconnected. |
| Maker request still pending | Wait or inspect server/OpenCode state. Current UI cannot safely interrupt it. | Do not assume the slow banner means failure. |
| OpenCode unavailable/auth failure | Correct the server URL/password outside persisted project state, then re-probe. | Do not store provider/server secrets in `project.json` or browser storage. |
| Sentry unavailable | Continue local operation and record telemetry as unverified. | Do not treat lack of telemetry as proof that no failure occurred. |

## Phase obligations

- Phase 1 implements durable in-flight operations, native interruption, restart reconciliation, and retention for run events before it changes Maker behavior.
- The first phase that changes schema v1 implements the migration/backup rules above before writing user state.
- Phase 6 documents and verifies mode-specific backups and resets for local full, hosted demo, and private hosted deployments.
- Phase 8 completes locking, backup rotation, corruption quarantine, retention, incident response, budgets, secure cleanup, and recovery tests.
- Phase 9 exercises supported prior-version fixtures and links release evidence.

# OpenCode integration

Status: canonical implemented integration contract  
Last verified: 31 October 2026 (IST)

This document owns OpenCode-specific facts. It does not authorize provider login, account changes, inference, or credential handling.

## Supported baseline

| Item | Inspected fact | Compatibility statement |
|---|---|---|
| Node | `package.json` requires `>=22.14.0`; Render pins `22.14.0`; Phase 0 ran on `22.14.0` | Node 22.14.0 is the verified baseline. Later Node releases are not proven by Phase 0. |
| OpenCode client | `@opencode/client` is lockfile-pinned to `2.0.32` | 2.0.32 is the supported client baseline. |
| Hosted OpenCode binary | `@opencode/cli-linux-x64-baseline` is lockfile-pinned to `2.0.32` | Render starts this exact Linux x64 baseline package. |
| Local CLI | Safe preflight found `opencode 2.0.32` on PATH | CLI startup and `serve --help` passed; no server/model session was started. |
| Server response | `nativeEngineStatusSchema` accepts a version matching `2.x` | This broad validation is not evidence that every 2.x release is compatible. Re-verify before changing either pin. |
| Model | Hard-coded `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` | Availability, free pricing, and behavior are unstable external facts; Phase 0 did not perform inference. |

The preflight also found an adjacent legacy `@opencode-ai/sdk 1.18.26` and correctly marked it inconclusive. Application code imports only `@opencode/client`; the adjacent package is not the declared application contract.

## Connection and credential ownership

- Local OpenCode is expected at `OPENCODE_BASE_URL`, defaulting to `http://127.0.0.1:4096`.
- When `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` is set, the server sends HTTP Basic Auth using username `opencode`. OpenCode must be started with the matching server password.
- Provider/model credentials and provider login state belong to OpenCode. They are not copied into browser storage or project state.
- The application server reads the OpenCode password from its environment. The browser never receives it.
- Render starts OpenCode as a child process with matching `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` and `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD`, plus persistent XDG data/config directories.

Current operator steps remain in [SENTRY_AND_OPENCODE_SETUP.md](SENTRY_AND_OPENCODE_SETUP.md) until `docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md` is created with a verified onboarding flow.

## API surface used

The application currently uses:

- server information and model catalog for `/api/engine`;
- session create/get, prompt/generate/wait, and message list;
- session diff after Maker work; and
- session get/outcome for reconciliation.

Oracle, Architect, and Witness create read-only sessions in `spirit-workspace`. Maker creates an edit-capable, shell-denied session in `demo-workspace`. A saved session id is reused for Oracle, Architect, and Maker; Witness deliberately starts fresh for evidence review.

## Current operation behavior

- `speak` first calls synchronous generation. If the returned text is shorter than 80 characters, it sends a prompt, waits for idle with a 90-second deadline, and reconstructs assistant text from message history.
- `perform` prompts Maker and waits in the same API request for idle or a 180-second timer. It then checks model/cost and asks OpenCode for the session diff.
- A Maker timeout does not interrupt the native session. If no diff is visible, the operation is stored as failed; network-like failures are stored as `UNKNOWN` but may lack a native session id.
- The current cancel endpoint changes only application state for a stored non-terminal operation. It does not invoke an OpenCode abort/interrupt API.
- Reconciliation calls session get and maps native succeeded/failed/interrupted/running/idle information to the saved application operation. No event subscription is used.

## Authentication and failure states

| Failure | Current signal | Recovery today |
|---|---|---|
| Server stopped/wrong URL | Engine 503 or network-like operation error | Start OpenCode or correct server environment, then make a new request only when no unknown operation needs reconciliation. |
| Missing/wrong password | OpenCode request failure | Match `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` with the OpenCode server password and retry. The UI does not yet identify auth separately. |
| Model absent | `modelAvailable: false` with a fixed-model limitation | Configure OpenCode so the exact model appears. Substitution is rejected. |
| Model/cost changes during a session | Operation throws after session inspection | Inspect OpenCode/provider state; do not claim a free successful run. |
| Timeout/disconnect | Application records `UNKNOWN` when classified as network-like | Reconcile only when a native session id was saved; do not blindly repeat. |
| Malformed model output | Schema error; bounded Architect/Witness prose fallback in some cases | Revise/retry without treating text as approval. |

## Trust and privacy

- OpenCode and its configured model provider receive runtime prompts and the selected workshop context. “Local browser” does not mean inference stays on the device.
- Model output, messages, errors, and diffs are untrusted. Zod schemas and workflow transitions—not model prose—control approval and stage changes.
- Native permissions are defense-in-depth around workspace selection. The checked-in fixture test validates its fixture shape, but Phase 0 did not repeat a live OpenCode edit/denial proof.
- Sentry agent spans record role, conversation/session/message identifiers, model name, cost metadata, and tool names. Instrumentation disables GenAI inputs/outputs and request secrets.

## Re-verification triggers

Re-run official API/version checks and an opt-in live compatibility diagnostic before changing the OpenCode/client version, permission shape, session/event APIs, model/provider policy, authentication method, timeout/retry policy, or hosted process model. Record the result here, the system effect in Architecture, setup impact in Local Setup/Hosted Deployment, recovery impact in Operations, and the release note in Changelog.
# Operations and recovery

Status: canonical state, backup, migration, and recovery policy  
Last verified: 31 October 2026 (IST)

This document owns persisted-state operations. The rules below are binding prerequisites for later schema changes; Phase 0 does not alter user data or implement a migration runner.

## Current persisted state

`UB_DATA_DIR` defaults to `.unfinished-business/`. The application currently manages:

```text
UB_DATA_DIR/
  project.json
  project.json.previous
  demo-workspace/
  spirit-workspace/
```

Render additionally keeps OpenCode XDG data and config under `/var/data`. Secrets remain environment-owned and are not part of a repository backup.

`project.json` uses `schemaVersion: 1` and a monotonically increasing `revision`. Its validated record contains project identity/workspace, workflow stage, sections and approvals, idempotent actions, operations, evidence, next action, product and Maker approvals, capped transcript, capabilities, Witness drafts, and native session references.

Current saves are temporary-file-plus-rename writes with a one-generation `.previous` copy. Current loads fall back to `.previous` when the primary file cannot be parsed or validated. This is crash recovery, not a sufficient backup or migration system.

Phase 0 validated the existing local primary record read-only as schema v1/revision 6 and the previous snapshot as schema v1/revision 5. It did not print user text, migrate, repair, or write either file. This is inspection evidence, not a promise that those revisions remain current after later application use.

## Versioning rules

1. `schemaVersion` is a required positive integer at the root of every durable project record. Version 1 remains the only implemented version in Phase 0.
2. A code change that changes required fields, field meaning, enum meaning, identity, or durable invariants must increment the schema version. Adding a Zod default alone does not waive migration review.
3. Migrations are forward-only, explicit, deterministic functions `N -> N+1`. The application must chain them one version at a time and validate after every step.
4. A migration must preserve ids, approvals, hashes, revisions, evidence provenance, operation/native-session references, and user text unless the corresponding decision entry explicitly documents a loss and recovery path.
5. Unsupported newer versions fail closed with an actionable message. They must never be coerced into an older schema or overwritten.
6. Migration code performs no inference, network requests, provider login, deployment action, or external account mutation.
7. A migration is complete only with fixtures for every supported source version, success tests, interrupted-write recovery, corrupt-input preservation, idempotent restart behavior, and documented rollback limits.

## Backup-before-migration rules

Before the first write by code that can migrate durable state:

1. Stop mutations or acquire an exclusive data-directory lock.
2. Read bytes without modifying the source and validate/detect the source version.
3. Create a uniquely named, timestamped backup outside the replacement path. Include `project.json`, its `.previous` snapshot, and any workspace/native metadata whose identifiers the migrated record references. For a private hosted instance, take a provider disk/snapshot backup when supported as well.
4. Record the source schema, application version/commit, size, and a cryptographic checksum in a backup manifest. Never include environment secrets in that manifest.
5. Verify the backup can be read before migration continues.
6. Write the migrated record to a new temporary file, validate it completely, flush it as supported, and atomically rename it into place. Preserve corrupt or rejected inputs under a quarantine name; never overwrite them with a default project.
7. Keep the migration backup until the new version has passed its documented validation window. Retention and pruning must be explicit and must never delete the last known-good backup.

The existing `project.json.previous` file does not satisfy these rules: it has no unique generation, manifest, checksum, retention guarantee, or workspace/OpenCode coverage.

## Forward migration and rollback

- Startup may automatically migrate only versions explicitly listed as supported by the running build. It must surface that a backup and migration occurred.
- If any step fails, leave the original and backup untouched, quarantine partial output, and refuse mutations. Do not initialize a blank project over recoverable data.
- Rollback means stopping the application and restoring a verified pre-migration backup with the application version that understands it. Never run older code against state already written by newer code.
- A successful migration is not reversed in place. Corrections are a new forward migration.
- OpenCode session ids may outlive application migration but are external references; inability to inspect an old session must become an honest limitation, not deletion of local evidence.

## Current recovery matrix

| Symptom | Safe current action | Do not do |
|---|---|---|
| `project.json` invalid but `.previous` valid | Stop writes, copy both files to an operator backup, inspect the load source, and restore deliberately. | Do not delete the primary or assume fallback is a migration. |
| Both project files invalid | Preserve both and logs, stop the app, and diagnose against schema v1. | Do not let startup replace them with a new project. |
| Revision conflict | Reload project state and reapply the user's intended change to the new revision. | Do not bypass the expected revision. |
| Duplicate action id/same payload | Treat the returned state as the idempotent result. | Do not invoke OpenCode again. |
| Duplicate action id/different payload | Generate a new action id after reviewing intent. | Do not reuse the id or overwrite its ledger entry. |
| Native operation unknown | Reconcile the saved native session before retrying. | Do not start a duplicate run merely because the browser disconnected. |
| Maker request still pending | Wait or inspect server/OpenCode state. Current UI cannot safely interrupt it. | Do not assume the slow banner means failure. |
| OpenCode unavailable/auth failure | Correct the server URL/password outside persisted project state, then re-probe. | Do not store provider/server secrets in `project.json` or browser storage. |
| Sentry unavailable | Continue local operation and record telemetry as unverified. | Do not treat lack of telemetry as proof that no failure occurred. |

## Phase obligations

- Phase 1 implements durable in-flight operations, native interruption, restart reconciliation, and retention for run events before it changes Maker behavior.
- The first phase that changes schema v1 implements the migration/backup rules above before writing user state.
- Phase 6 documents and verifies mode-specific backups and resets for local full, hosted demo, and private hosted deployments.
- Phase 8 completes locking, backup rotation, corruption quarantine, retention, incident response, budgets, secure cleanup, and recovery tests.
- Phase 9 exercises supported prior-version fixtures and links release evidence.

      })
      .catch((caught: unknown) => {
        setError(caught instanceof Error ? caught.message : "The workshop could not be loaded.");
      });
  }, []);

  async function act(work: () => Promise<{ project: WorkshopProject }>) {
    setBusy(true);
    setError(null);
    try {
      setProject((await work()).project);
    } catch (caught) {
      const loaded = await loadProject().catch(() => null);
      if (loaded) setProject(loaded);
      setError(caught instanceof ApiError
        ? `${caught.message} ${caught.retryable ? "You can try a new request. The current section was not overwritten." : "Nothing was repeated."}`
        : "The workshop lost its connection. Reload before trying again.");
    } finally {
      setBusy(false);
    }
  }

  async function actOnRun(work: () => Promise<RunActionResult>) {
    setBusy(true);
    setError(null);
    setRunError(null);
    try {
      const result = await work();
      setProject(result.project);
      setSelectedRunId(result.run.id);
      setSelectedRun(result.run);
      runCursor.current = result.run.lastEventSequence;
      sessionStorage.setItem(`ub-run-cursor:${result.run.id}`, String(runCursor.current));
    } catch (caught) {
      const loaded = await loadProject().catch(() => null);
      if (loaded) setProject(loaded);
      setError(caught instanceof ApiError
        ? `${caught.message} ${caught.retryable ? "You can retry after reviewing the saved run." : "Nothing was repeated."}`
        : "The Maker action lost its connection. Inspect the saved run before retrying.");
    } finally {
      setBusy(false);
    }
  }

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!selectedRunId) return;
    const abort = new AbortController();
    let stopped = false;
    const connect = async () => {
      while (!stopped && !abort.signal.aborted) {
        try {
          await streamRunEvents(selectedRunId, runCursor.current, abort.signal, (item) => {
            if (item.type === "heartbeat") return;
            const run = item.run;
            setSelectedRun(run);
            runCursor.current = item.type === "event" ? item.event.sequence : run.lastEventSequence;
            sessionStorage.setItem(`ub-run-cursor:${selectedRunId}`, String(runCursor.current));
            setRunError(null);
            if (["SUCCEEDED", "FAILED", "CANCELLED"].includes(run.status)) {
              void loadProject().then(setProject).catch(() => undefined);
            }
          });
          return;
        } catch (caught) {
          if (abort.signal.aborted) return;
          setRunError(caught instanceof Error ? caught.message : "Run Inspector disconnected.");
          await new Promise((resolve) => window.setTimeout(resolve, 1_000));
        }
      }
    };
    void connect();
    return () => {
      stopped = true;
      abort.abort();
    };
  }, [selectedRunId]);

  if (!project) {
    return (
      <main className="workshop">
        <h1>Unfinished Business</h1>
        <p>{error ?? "The workshop is waking up."}</p>
      </main>
    );
  }

  const section = project.sections.find((item) => item.id === project.currentSectionId) ?? null;
  const unknown = project.runs.find((item) => item.status === "UNKNOWN") ?? null;
  const header = project.stage === "ORACLE"
    ? "What's still haunting your to-do list?"
    : section
      ? `${section.title} — section ${section.order} of ${project.sections.length}`
      : project.nextAction;

  return (
    <>
      <a className="skip" href="#document">Skip to the working document</a>
      <main className="workshop">
        <nav className="stage-strip" aria-label="Spirits">
          {spirits.map(([id, label, Icon]) => {
            const done = stageOrder(project.stage) > stageOrder(id);
            return (
              <button key={id} type="button" className={done ? "stage done" : "stage"} aria-current={project.stage === id ? "step" : undefined} disabled>
                <Icon aria-hidden="true" size={18} />
                {label}
              </button>
            );
          })}
        </nav>
        <div className="frame">
          <aside className="side">
            <section className="panel">
              <h2>Outline</h2>
              <ol>
                {project.sections.map((item) => (
                  <li key={item.id} className={item.status === "STALE" ? "ghost" : undefined}>
                    {item.title} — {statusLabel(item)}
                  </li>
                ))}
              </ol>
            </section>
          </aside>
          <article className="document" id="document" aria-busy={busy}>
            <Lantern />
            <p className="eyebrow">{project.stage}</p>
            <h1>
              {header}
              {project.product.status === "APPROVED" && section?.status === "APPROVED" ? (
                <Seal label="Approved" reduceMotion={reduceMotion} />
              ) : null}
            </h1>
            <p className="status-line">Stopped here: {project.nextAction}</p>
            {engine && !engine.available ? (
              <p className="banner bad" role="status">
                {engine.limitation?.includes("fetch failed")
                  ? "OpenCode is not reachable on the configured loopback address."
                  : engine.limitation}{" "}
                Start OpenCode, then try again. No paid model will be used.
              </p>
            ) : null}
            {unknown ? (
              <p className="banner bad" role="status">
                A native run is unknown and was not repeated.
                <button className="action secondary" type="button" disabled={busy} onClick={() => void actOnRun(() => reconcileRun(project, unknown.id))}>Reconcile native session</button>
              </p>
            ) : null}
            {error ? <p className="banner bad" role="alert">{error}</p> : null}

            {project.stage === "ORACLE" ? (
              <OraclePanel project={project} text={text} setText={setText} busy={busy} act={act} />
            ) : null}
            {project.stage === "ARCHITECT" && section ? (
              <ArchitectPanel
                project={project}
                section={section}
                change={change}
                setChange={setChange}
                text={text}
                setText={setText}
                busy={busy}
                act={act}
                reduceMotion={reduceMotion}
              />
              />
            ) : null}
            {project.stage === "ARCHITECT" && !section ? (
              <ScopePanel project={project} scope={scope} setScope={setScope} busy={busy} act={act} />
            ) : null}
            {project.stage === "MAKER" ? (
              <MakerPanel project={project} run={selectedRun} busy={busy} start={() => actOnRun(() => runMaker(project))} />
            ) : null}
            {project.stage === "WITNESS" ? (
              <WitnessPanel project={project} text={text} setText={setText} busy={busy} act={act} exportNote={exportNote} setExportNote={setExportNote} />
            ) : null}
            {selectedRun ? (
              <RunInspector
                project={project}
                run={selectedRun}
                busy={busy}
                streamError={runError}
                cancel={() => actOnRun(() => cancelRun(project, selectedRun.id))}
                reconcile={() => actOnRun(() => reconcileRun(project, selectedRun.id))}
                retry={() => actOnRun(() => runMaker(project))}
              />
            ) : null}
          </article>
          <aside className="side">
            <Activity project={project} />
          </aside>
        </div>
      </main>
    </>
  );
}

function RunInspector(props: {
  project: WorkshopProject;
  run: MakerRun;
  busy: boolean;
  streamError: string | null;
  cancel: () => void;
  reconcile: () => void;
  retry: () => void;
}) {
  const [now, setNow] = useState(Date.now());
  useEffect(() => {
    if (["SUCCEEDED", "FAILED", "CANCELLED"].includes(props.run.status)) return;
    const timer = window.setInterval(() => setNow(Date.now()), 1_000);
    return () => window.clearInterval(timer);
  }, [props.run.status]);
  const terminal = ["SUCCEEDED", "FAILED", "CANCELLED"].includes(props.run.status);
  const elapsed = Math.max(0, (props.run.finishedAt ? Date.parse(props.run.finishedAt) : now) - Date.parse(props.run.startedAt ?? props.run.createdAt));
  const last = props.run.events.at(-1);
  return (
    <section className="run-inspector" aria-live="polite" aria-label="Run Inspector">
      <div className="run-inspector-heading">
        <div>
          <p className="eyebrow">Run Inspector</p>
          <h2>Maker · {props.run.status.replaceAll("_", " ")}</h2>
        </div>
        <span className="meta">{formatDuration(elapsed)} elapsed</span>
      </div>
      <p>{last?.summary ?? "The saved run has no events yet."}</p>
      {props.streamError ? <p className="banner bad">Live updates disconnected: {props.streamError} Reconnecting from event {props.run.lastEventSequence}.</p> : null}
      {props.run.failureCode === "AUTHENTICATION" ? (
        <p className="banner bad">Repair OpenCode authentication by matching `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` with the server password, then reconcile or start a new run.</p>
      ) : null}
      <ol className="run-events">
        {props.run.events.slice(-50).map((event) => (
          <li key={event.id}>
            <span className="meta">#{event.sequence} · {event.category} · {new Date(event.timestamp).toLocaleTimeString()}</span>
            <div>{event.summary}</div>
          </li>
        ))}
      </ol>
      {props.run.result ? (
        <div className="run-evidence">
          <h3>Final evidence</h3>
          <p>{props.run.result.summary}</p>
          {props.run.result.files.length ? (
            <ul>{props.run.result.files.map((file) => <li key={file.path}>{file.status} {file.path} (+{file.additions}/-{file.deletions})</li>)}</ul>
          ) : <p>No file-change evidence is available.</p>}
          {props.run.result.verification ? (
            <p>Verification: {props.run.result.verification.status} · exit {props.run.result.verification.exitCode ?? "unavailable"}</p>
          ) : <p>Verification evidence is unavailable.</p>}
          {props.run.result.model ? <p>Model: {props.run.result.model.providerID}/{props.run.result.model.id} · cost {props.run.result.cost ?? "unknown"}</p> : null}
          {props.run.result.limitation ? <p className="banner">Limitation: {props.run.result.limitation}</p> : null}
        </div>
      ) : null}
      <div className="actions">
        {!terminal && props.run.status !== "UNKNOWN" ? (
          <button className="action secondary" type="button" disabled={props.busy || Boolean(props.run.cancelRequestedAt)} onClick={props.cancel}>
            {props.run.cancelRequestedAt ? "Cancellation pending" : "Cancel native run"}
          </button>
        ) : null}
        {props.run.status === "UNKNOWN" ? (
          <button className="action" type="button" disabled={props.busy} onClick={props.reconcile}>Reconcile saved session</button>
        ) : null}
        {(props.run.status === "FAILED" || props.run.status === "CANCELLED") && props.project.stage === "MAKER" ? (
          <button className="action" type="button" disabled={props.busy} onClick={props.retry}>Start a new run</button>
        ) : null}
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}

function formatDuration(milliseconds: number): string {
  const seconds = Math.floor(milliseconds / 1_000);
  const minutes = Math.floor(seconds / 60);
  return minutes ? `${minutes}m ${seconds % 60}s` : `${seconds}s`;
}

+

+
+```bash
+npm ci
+cp .env.example .env
+```

+OPENCODE_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4096

# Local setup

Status: canonical local prerequisites and start procedure  
Last verified: 31 October 2026 (IST)

This document owns the shortest supported local setup. Sentry account/release details remain in the legacy [SENTRY_AND_OPENCODE_SETUP.md](SENTRY_AND_OPENCODE_SETUP.md) until Phase 9 migration.

## Supported baseline

- Node `22.14.0` or a compatible `>=22.14.0` release; automated proof used `22.14.0`.
- npm `10.9.2` for the verified baseline.
- OpenCode server/client `2.0.32`. The application packages are lockfile-pinned; the local `opencode` CLI inspected by preflight was also `2.0.32`.
- The exact configured model is `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`. Availability and provider terms are external facts and must be checked in OpenCode. The application rejects substitution or non-zero native session cost.

## Install and configure

```bash
npm ci
cp .env.example .env
```

Keep `.env` private. At minimum, review:

```dotenv
OPENCODE_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4096
OPENCODE_PASSWORD=
UB_HOST=127.0.0.1
UB_PORT=4200
UB_DATA_DIR=.unfinished-business
```

Start OpenCode separately using its supported `serve` command. If the OpenCode server has a password, put the same value in `OPENCODE_PASSWORD`; the application uses Basic Auth user `opencode`. Provider authentication stays in OpenCode and is never copied into browser or project state.

The application must be the only process writing a given `UB_DATA_DIR`. OpenCode must be able to access the resolved `<UB_DATA_DIR>/demo-workspace`; Maker edits are confined there by workspace selection and deny shell/external-directory permissions.

## Start

Development:

```bash
npm run dev
```

Production-style local build:

```bash
npm run build
npm start
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:4200` unless `UB_HOST` or `UB_PORT` was changed. The browser obtains a workshop session token only on loopback unless hosted Basic Auth is configured.

## Verify the baseline

```bash
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
node scripts/preflight.mjs
```

Preflight does not perform inference or prove credentials, provider quota, events, permissions, interruption, or external telemetry. Automated tests use deterministic OpenCode fakes and temporary data directories.

## First startup after Phase 1

If `project.json` is schema v1, startup creates and verifies `project.json.backup-v1-<timestamp>-<checksum>.json` plus its manifest before atomically writing schema v2. Do not delete that backup. See [OPERATIONS_AND_RECOVERY.md](OPERATIONS_AND_RECOVERY.md) before restoring or moving state.

Non-terminal Maker runs are reconciled on startup. They are never automatically prompted again. Keep the same OpenCode data/config and server endpoint if an old native session must be inspected.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Check |
|---|---|
| Engine unavailable | Confirm OpenCode is listening at `OPENCODE_BASE_URL`. |
| Authentication failure | Match `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` to the OpenCode server password; never paste it into the browser. |
| Required model missing | Inspect OpenCode's model catalog/provider login for the exact supported model. Do not substitute silently. |
| Run is `UNKNOWN` | Use **Reconcile saved session** in Run Inspector before retrying. A local timeout deliberately leaves the native session alone. |
| Cancellation remains unknown | Restore OpenCode connectivity/authentication, then reconcile. Only observed native interruption is `CANCELLED`. |
| Revision conflict | Reload the page/project and repeat the intended user action with fresh state. |
| State migration fails | Stop the app, preserve primary/previous/backup/manifest files, and follow Operations and Recovery. Do not initialize over them. |

Sentry variables are optional for local function. Their absence means external telemetry is unverified, not that an operation succeeded.
